what_happened: The design job "Design per-job landing branches cut from main" was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier raised one major finding and no blockers: CHANGELOG.md is an expected deliverable and the changelog default applies, but the change did not modify it. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Only the verifier caught the gap, at the end.
cause: The changelog default is a rule the producer must remember, and no code compares the diff's file list with the expected deliverables before the verdict. For doc-only design jobs the changelog feels optional, so it is easy to skip. The reading and plan do not list the changelog as a visible deliverable. Only the verifier sees the gap, at the end, so a purely mechanical omission costs a whole job.
prevention: Add a code check that runs before the verifier. When the changelog default applies to a job, it fails fast if the diff does not touch CHANGELOG.md. It should report the missing file to the producer, which gets a repair round. The reading should also always list the changelog entry as a named deliverable when the default applies. This stops the whole class: no job reaches the final verdict without the entry.
proposed_request: Add a pre-verifier check to Athena. When the changelog default applies to a job, the check must confirm the job's diff modifies CHANGELOG.md. If it does not, the producer is told the specific missing file and gets one repair round before the verifier runs. Make the accepted reading list the changelog entry as a deliverable whenever the default applies. Acceptance: (1) a job with the default applying and no CHANGELOG.md change is stopped before the verifier with a message naming CHANGELOG.md; (2) a job that edits CHANGELOG.md passes the check; (3) a job where the default does not apply, such as a records-only change, is not affected; (4) tests cover all three cases. Then re-ask: Design per-job landing branches cut from main, with a CHANGELOG.md entry.
